headline: AI designs viruses that kill bacteria

sources.title: AI used to create viruses not found in nature for first time
AI designs synthetic virus in scientific first, raising biosecurity concerns
Stanford scientists just used AI to build a virus to target E. coli
Scientists create new viruses with AI, raising alarms about the future of biosecurity (video, CBS News)

chunks.text: Researchers at Stanford University trained an AI model on millions of [[genomes]] from across nature. They {{built on}} one real virus as a [[template]] and asked the model for new ones. It {{churned out}} thousands of designs. About 300 were {{tried out}} in a [[lab]], and 16 of them worked. The [[study]] {{came out}} in the journal Science on August 6 and was [[peer-reviewed]].

chunks.text: The new viruses are [[phages]], which attack [[bacteria]] and are [[harmless]] to people. Phages {{go after}} one kind of germ and leave the rest alone. In the lab these ones {{wiped out}} E. coli, including [[strains]] that a natural phage cannot kill. Doctors hope the method will {{break through}} where [[antibiotics]] no longer work. The tests were run on cells in dishes, not in animals and not in people.

chunks.text: A [[commentary]] printed beside the study said the tools to write a viral genome now exist while the rules to control them do not. Biosecurity experts {{called for}} limits before the method spreads. The team says it {{left out}} viruses that [[infect]] humans when it trained the model, so the system has never seen one. Governments have not yet {{drawn up}} rules of their own.

chunks.text: The argument is about speed. Written rules {{fall behind}} laboratory work that moves this fast. Some scientists want to {{rein in}} the most powerful models until safety checks exist, and others want governments to {{clamp down}} on who is allowed to use them. But [[drug-resistant]] bacteria already kill more than a million people a year, so waiting also has a [[price]].

mainIdea.s: Scientists at Stanford used an AI model to design brand new viruses that are not found in nature. In lab tests some of these viruses killed bacteria strains that an ordinary phage cannot kill.
mainIdea.why: The study found that AI-designed phages killed E. coli, including strains that natural phages cannot beat, and it came out in Science on August 6.

mainIdea.s: The new AI-made viruses were tested on animals and shown to be completely safe for human patients. Doctors plan to use them right away to treat drug-resistant infections in hospitals.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the tests were run only on cells in a lab dish, not on animals or people, so nobody has used them as medicine yet.

mainIdea.s: Health regulators say a new class of antibiotics has just entered human trials to fight drug-resistant infections. The drug works differently from phages and does not rely on any AI model.
mainIdea.why: This story is about a different antibiotic drug in human trials, not about the AI-designed viruses called phages.
